skill.name: cargo-project
skill.description: Manage a whole Cargo workspace as code — declare connectors, models, plays, tools, agents, MCP servers, segments, context, folders, files, workers, and apps in TypeScript, then reconcile them with `cargo-ai project` (init → types → plan → deploy), the way you would run Pulumi or the AWS CDK. Triggers: "as code", "in git", "version-controlled", "reproducible", "Terraform for Cargo", "set up a whole workspace", "staging and production", "deploy the workspace from CI", "review this in a PR", "cargo.state.json", "scaffold from a template", "is there a cookbook for this", "start from a cookbook". Skills with a CDK example (TAM building, account scoring, call capture, inbound qualification, CRM enrichment, standup) live in gtm-skills; menu in references/cookbooks.md. Skip when: it is a one-off operation, a read, or an ad-hoc query — use the matching capability skill.
skill.summary: Define, review, and deploy Cargo workspace resources from a version-controlled TypeScript project.
skill.author: getcargohq

security_audit.summary: All 271 static alerts are false positives involving documentation formatting, fixed local imports, expected credential placeholders, and Cargo resource identifiers. One semantic risk remains: pull-request preview guidance treats imported TypeScript as safe without requiring isolation from credentials or privileged runners. No evidence found of prompt injection, credential exfiltration, or malicious payloads in the reviewed files.

remediation.issue: Pull-request planning executes project modules, but the CI recipe calls previews safe without defining a trust boundary.
remediation.suggestion: Document import-time execution and require isolated, unprivileged preview runners without secrets, cached authentication, or write tokens; approve untrusted changes before privileged execution.

Side branches: `cargo-ai project check` (validate the tree, no state, no API calls —
the CI/editor subset of `plan`) · `cargo-ai project info` (what is here: every declared
resource, the file that declared it, whether it is deployed) · `cargo-ai project refresh`
(read-only drift report) · `deploy --refresh` (re-apply code over out-of-band edits) ·
`deploy --prune` (delete resources removed from code) · `cargo-ai project import <id> <uuid>`
(bind an existing live resource into state) · `cargo-ai project pull` (generate `define*`
source from a live workspace and adopt it) · `cargo-ai project rollback` (restore the
pre-deploy state snapshot) · `cargo-ai project state` (inspect and repoint the deploy state).
**`plan` and `info` answer different questions.** `plan` answers *what will deploy do* —
its unit is the change, and it exits non-zero so CI can gate on it. `info` answers *what
is here* — its unit is the resource, and it never fails. `check` is `plan` minus the diff:
project` with no arguments does `info` inside a project and `init` outside one.

semantic_findings.title: Pull-Request Previews Lack a Code-Execution Trust Boundary
semantic_findings.description: The CI recipe says "Preview safely" on pull requests, while the loader imports project TypeScript and runs module side effects. Untrusted changes can execute before deployment approval and access runner credentials or files unless previews use isolated, unprivileged environments.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The documentation directly establishes import-time execution and recommends pull-request previews without isolation requirements. No exploit is shown; credential exposure depends on runner permissions.

content.user_title: Manage Cargo Workspaces as TypeScript Projects
content.value_statement: Manual workspace changes are difficult to review and reproduce across environments. This skill guides TypeScript resource definitions, deployment previews, and state management with Cargo.
actual_capabilities: Guide project scaffolding and cookbook installation with cargo-ai project init and project add.
Help define connectors, models, workflows, agents, MCP servers, hosted apps, and workers using Cargo CDK builders.
Wire resource dependencies through handles and generate configuration types from workspace integration schemas.
Explain deployment plans, confirmation, pruning, drift refresh, and state recovery.
Guide adoption of existing resources through import, pull, and deploy-state binding.
Describe CI token authentication, environment secrets, and separate deployment states for different workspaces.
limitations: Execution requires the Cargo CLI, project dependencies, a Cargo account, and appropriate workspace permissions.
Planning imports project TypeScript; it is not a sandbox for untrusted code.
Workflow callbacks support a restricted JavaScript subset, not arbitrary asynchronous application logic.
The entrypoint warns that cookbook examples are not yet live-deploy verified; rollback restores state, not completed API changes.

use_cases.title: Version-Control a Revenue Workspace
use_cases.description: Declare CRM connectors, data models, and automation together so workspace changes can receive code review before deployment.

use_cases.title: Deploy Across Environments
use_cases.description: Configure protected-branch deployments with workspace-scoped tokens and separate state pointers for staging and production.

use_cases.title: Adopt Existing Cargo Resources
use_cases.description: Bring live models and agents under project management without creating duplicate resources.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Cargo Project
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me scaffold a Cargo project in an empty directory. Confirm the workspace, explain dependencies, and stop after showing the deployment plan.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: create a first version-controlled project.

prompt_templates.title: Connect a CRM Data Model
prompt_templates.prompt: Add a HubSpot connector and contacts model to my Cargo project. Use secret() for credentials, wire dependencies by handle, and request approval before deployment.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: add a connected data source and model.

prompt_templates.title: Adopt a Live Agent
prompt_templates.prompt: Bring my existing Cargo agent under project management. Inspect its dependencies, bind its live UUID, and verify the plan avoids duplicate creation.

prompt_templates.title: Design Protected CI Deployment
prompt_templates.prompt: Design staging and production deployment jobs with separate states and scoped tokens. Isolate untrusted previews without secrets and require approval for pruning or paid schedules.

output_examples.input: Add a HubSpot connector and contacts model, then show what would change.
output: Proposed resources: a HubSpot connector and a contacts model linked through the connector handle.
Credential setup: provide HUBSPOT_API_KEY through the deployment environment, not source control.
Review checkpoint: create the connector before the model, inspect the plan, and wait for deployment approval.

output_examples.input: Help me manage an existing agent without creating another copy.
output: Adoption checklist: identify the live agent UUID and declare its connector, model, and tool dependencies.
State mapping: bind the declared agent identifier to the existing live resource.
Verification: the plan should show an update or no change, not a new agent.

output_examples.input: Review my deployment approach for staging and production.
output: Environment separation: use distinct workspace tokens and deploy-state pointers.
Preview boundary: run untrusted project imports only in isolated runners without secrets or write permissions.
Deployment gate: allow protected-branch changes after review, with explicit approval for deletions and recurring costs.

best_practices: Review project code and deployment plans before approval; isolate untrusted previews from credentials and privileged runners.
Commit the deploy-state pointer, ignore generated working files, and maintain separate states for different environments.
Use secret() or workspaceEnv() for credentials, wire dependencies by handle, and approve recurring costs before enabling schedules.
anti_patterns: Running unreviewed project TypeScript on an authenticated machine or privileged CI runner.
Using forced initialization in a nonempty project or deleting its deploy-state pointer to reset deployment.
Treating prune, destroy, DNS replacement, or paid schedules as routine changes without explicit review.

faq.question: Does this skill manage Rust Cargo projects?
faq.answer: No. It manages Cargo platform workspaces through the cargo-ai CLI and TypeScript CDK.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The skill declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code. Command execution also requires the Cargo CLI and project dependencies.

faq.question: Can I preview changes without deploying?
faq.answer: Yes. project plan previews resource changes, and project check validates definitions. Both load project code, so untrusted inputs require isolation.

faq.question: Where should credentials be stored?
faq.answer: Use deployment environment secrets with secret(), or supported workspace catalog references with workspaceEnv(). Keep credential values out of source control.

faq.question: What should I commit for deployment state?
faq.answer: Commit cargo.state.json, which points to workspace-held state in current projects. Ignore generated working files and coordinate migration from older inline state.

faq.question: Does rollback undo changes in the live workspace?
faq.answer: No. Rollback restores the deployment-state snapshot. Correct the resource definitions and deploy again to address live changes.
